q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a fibre cement roof sheet?
title: Fibre cement sheet carbon footprint per sheet
short: Cement is the main input: multiply the cement per sheet by the cement maker's per-kg figure. Add fibre, fly ash and the plant's forming, steam curing and electricity, then divide by sheets made and report by length and thickness.

ul: Curing with steam or air, and trimming.

p: Report per sheet with length and thickness, and per square metre for comparison with metal roofing.

example.title: Worked example: fibre cement roof sheet unit per sheet (one month)
lines: Plant total: 132,300 / 60,000 = 2.205 kg CO2 per sheet
Add cement and fibre for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
